title: Morning Inbox
intro: Busy morning, Toddy. Ten messages, one minute.
Swipe left if it's a scam, right if it's safe. Or tap the buttons.
Careful: some of them are honest. Don't cry wolf.

cards.text: Your account is LOCKED. Verify within 1 hour: zelvora-secure.co/login
cards.why: Look-alike link plus a deadline. Real apps tell you to open the app, not a strange link.

cards.text: Planned maintenance tonight, 1–2 AM. Swaps pause for an hour. No action needed.
cards.why: The official handle with Plenvo's real badge, and it asks you for nothing.

cards.text: You won the community raffle! 🎉 Send 10 ZLV to cover the fee and claim your prize.
cards.why: Real prizes never cost money to claim, and admins don't DM winners asking for coins.

cards.text: Movie night Friday? I'll bring the popcorn 🍿
cards.why: A friend you know, asking for nothing. Not every message is a trap.

cards.text: We detected suspicious activity. Reply with your recovery phrase so we can secure your funds.
cards.why: No real support ever asks for your recovery phrase, whatever the reason.

cards.text: New login from Lisbon. If this wasn't you, open the Hedrio app and go to Security.
cards.why: From the real domain, no link to click, and it sends you to the app you already have.

cards.text: 🎁 Free airdrop waiting for you! Claim at kelvaro-airdrop.claim-now.xyz. Only 5 min left!
cards.why: Unknown sender, strange link, and a countdown. Free money that expires in minutes is bait.

cards.text: Earn €250 a day just liking posts! Pay €49 registration and start today.
cards.why: Real jobs never make you pay to start. Easy money for likes is a task scam.

cards.text: 482913 is your Zelvora login code. Never share this code with anyone, not even Zelvora staff.
cards.why: You just logged in, and the message itself warns you never to share the code. Use it, don't share it.

cards.text: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone 😭 this is my new number. Can you send €800 urgently? I'll explain later.
cards.why: A new number plus an urgent money request. Call the old number first to check it's really them.

golden_rule: Urgent plus money, codes or links means stop and check. Calm messages that ask for nothing are usually fine.

quick_check.q: A text from a new number says it's your cousin and needs money urgently. What's the best first step?

options.text: Send a small amount, just in case
Call your cousin's old number to check
Reply asking them to prove it

quick_check.explain: Check through a way you already trust. A scammer can answer questions; they can't answer your cousin's real phone.
